chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him), saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade me from wearing a gold ring, from wearing silk clothes, from wearing red garments, from using thick blankets, and from reciting the Quran while bowing.
The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: 'Silk clothes' refers to clothes brought from Egypt that are mixed with silk.
ai.seo_question: What are the five specific things the Prophet forbade Imam Ali from doing?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights five specific prohibitions (nahy) directed at Imam Ali (AS), reflecting the Shia scholarly distinction between general prohibitions for the Ummah and specific ones for the Ahl al-Bayt. The compiler, Shaykh al-Saduq, clarifies that 'Qasi' refers to Egyptian fabrics mixed with silk, emphasizing the material nature of the restriction rather than a total ban on all fine textiles. These prohibitions underscore the unique spiritual and physical discipline required of the Imams, linking their conduct to the purity of worship as seen in the Quranic injunctions on prayer.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-49 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father -may God be pleased with him- narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad and Abdullahibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman, on the authority of al-Halabi, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that Ali (MGB) said, “The Prophet (MGB) has admonished us (Imams) against five things. I am not saying that he (MGB) has admonished you against them.

They are as follows: wearing a gold ring on the fingers; wearing silk clothes from Egypt; wearing red clothes; using highly reddish blankets; and reciting the Quran while bowing down.”The compiler of the book - may God be pleased with him - said, “What is meant by silk clothes from Egypt is clothes made from a fabric which is woven with silk and comes from Egypt.”
